types.stock: Shares of one specific company. Buying it makes you a part-owner of that exact business — with its successes and its struggles.
types.etf: A ready-made basket of many companies or assets in a single security. One click, and your money is instantly spread across the whole basket.
types.bondEtf: A basket of bonds — essentially many loans to governments or companies, packaged into one security with interest payments.
types.crypto: A digital currency that exists and trades without a central bank, built on blockchain technology. Usually noticeably more volatile than stocks.
types.fiat: An ordinary government-issued currency — the dollar, the euro, the yen, and so on — used in everyday life and the unit other assets are priced in.

NVDA.name: Nvidia
NVDA.text: Makes the chips that almost every major company uses to train AI models and to power video games.

MSFT.name: Microsoft
MSFT.text: Windows, Office, the Azure cloud, and one of the biggest investors in AI technology.

GOOGL.name: Alphabet (Google)
GOOGL.text: Google Search, YouTube, Android, and one of the world's largest advertising machines.

META.name: Meta Platforms
META.text: Owns Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp — earns most of its money from ads inside those apps.

AMD.name: Advanced Micro Devices
AMD.text: Makes processors and graphics cards — the main rival to Intel and Nvidia in the chip world.

PLTR.name: Palantir Technologies
PLTR.text: Builds big-data analytics software for governments and large businesses.

SMCI.name: Supermicro
SMCI.text: Builds servers and data-center hardware, including gear used for AI workloads.

ARKK.name: ARK Innovation ETF
ARKK.text: A fund that gathers companies betting on future technology — from AI to biotech.

JNJ.name: Johnson & Johnson
JNJ.text: One of the largest makers of medicines, medical products, and consumer health goods.

PG.name: Procter & Gamble
PG.text: Makes household products used in almost every home — from laundry detergent to diapers.

KO.name: Coca-Cola Company
KO.text: One of the most recognizable drinks in the world, plus dozens of other soda and juice brands.

VZ.name: Verizon
VZ.text: One of the largest mobile and internet carriers in the US.

T.name: AT&T
T.text: Another major American telecom carrier — connectivity and internet for millions of people.

MO.name: Altria
MO.text: A tobacco company (including Marlboro in the US), long known for steady dividends.

SCHD.name: Schwab US Dividend Equity ETF
SCHD.text: A fund that gathers US companies with a track record of steady, growing dividends.

VYM.name: Vanguard High Dividend Yield ETF
VYM.text: A fund made up of companies that traditionally pay higher dividends than the market average.

NEE.name: NextEra Energy
NEE.text: One of the largest US energy companies, actively expanding wind and solar generation.

ENPH.name: Enphase Energy
ENPH.text: Makes electronics for solar panels — inverters that turn sunlight into electricity for homes.

FSLR.name: First Solar
FSLR.text: One of the largest solar panel manufacturers in the US.

ICLN.name: iShares Global Clean Energy ETF
ICLN.text: A fund of companies from around the world tied to renewable energy.

TAN.name: Invesco Solar ETF
TAN.text: A fund focused specifically on the solar energy industry.

AAPL.name: Apple Inc.
AAPL.text: iPhone, Mac, Apple Watch, and a services ecosystem — one of the most valuable companies in the world.

AMZN.name: Amazon
AMZN.text: The world's largest online store and the AWS cloud service, which powers a huge share of the internet.

UNH.name: UnitedHealth Group
UNH.text: The largest health insurance and healthcare company in the US.

PFE.name: Pfizer
PFE.text: A major pharmaceutical company, known among other things for its COVID-19 vaccine.

MRK.name: Merck & Co.
MRK.text: A pharmaceutical giant developing medicines and vaccines worldwide.

ABBV.name: AbbVie
ABBV.text: A pharma company known in part for its treatments for immune-related diseases.

XLV.name: Health Care Select Sector SPDR Fund
XLV.text: A fund bundling the largest US healthcare companies into one package.

IBB.name: iShares Biotechnology ETF
IBB.text: A fund focused on biotechnology companies.

JPM.name: JPMorgan Chase
JPM.text: The largest US bank by assets.

BAC.name: Bank of America
BAC.text: One of the largest retail and investment banks in the US.

WFC.name: Wells Fargo
WFC.text: A major American bank with a nationwide branch network.

GS.name: Goldman Sachs
GS.text: One of the most well-known investment banks in the world.

MS.name: Morgan Stanley
MS.text: A large investment bank that also manages money for private clients.

V.name: Visa Inc.
V.text: A payment network that handles a huge share of card payments worldwide.

MA.name: Mastercard
MA.text: One of the two main global payment networks, alongside Visa.

XLF.name: Financial Select Sector SPDR Fund
XLF.text: A fund of the largest US banks and financial companies.

WMT.name: Walmart
WMT.text: The world's largest retail chain — supermarkets used by millions every day.

PEP.name: PepsiCo
PEP.text: Pepsi drinks and a huge portfolio of snacks like Lay's and Doritos.

MCD.name: McDonald's
MCD.text: The world's largest fast-food chain, with restaurants in nearly every country.

NKE.name: Nike, Inc.
NKE.text: One of the biggest global brands in sportswear and footwear.

XLP.name: Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR Fund
XLP.text: A fund of everyday consumer goods companies — food, drinks, household products.

INTC.name: Intel
INTC.text: One of the oldest and largest makers of computer processors.

AVGO.name: Broadcom
AVGO.text: Makes chips and networking equipment for telecom, data centers, and smartphones.

TXN.name: Texas Instruments
TXN.text: Makes simple but essential chips found inside an enormous range of devices.

SMH.name: VanEck Semiconductor ETF
SMH.text: A fund of the world's largest chipmakers and chip-equipment companies.

SOXX.name: iShares Semiconductor ETF
SOXX.text: Another fund gathering companies across the whole semiconductor industry.

TSLA.name: Tesla, Inc.
TSLA.text: A maker of electric vehicles and energy storage, one of the most talked-about names in the news.

GM.name: General Motors
GM.text: One of the largest traditional US automakers, also expanding into electric vehicles.

F.name: Ford Motor Company
F.text: A classic American automaker gradually expanding its electric vehicle lineup.

RIVN.name: Rivian Automotive
RIVN.text: A young maker of electric pickup trucks and SUVs.

LCID.name: Lucid Group
LCID.text: A young maker of premium electric vehicles.

BA.name: Boeing
BA.text: One of the two largest aircraft manufacturers in the world, also active in military and space technology.

LMT.name: Lockheed Martin
LMT.text: A major defense contractor, known among other things for military aircraft.

RTX.name: RTX Corporation
RTX.text: An aerospace and defense company that makes aircraft engines and defense systems.

NOC.name: Northrop Grumman
NOC.text: A defense contractor working on aviation and space programs, among other things.

CRWD.name: CrowdStrike
CRWD.text: A cybersecurity company that protects computers and networks from attacks.

PANW.name: Palo Alto Networks
PANW.text: One of the largest providers of cybersecurity solutions for businesses.

FTNT.name: Fortinet
FTNT.text: A company that makes hardware and software to protect corporate networks.

ZS.name: Zscaler
ZS.text: A cloud-based cybersecurity platform that protects remote work and company networks.

HACK.name: ETFMG Prime Cyber Security ETF
HACK.text: A fund that bundles cybersecurity companies into one package.

CIBR.name: First Trust NASDAQ Cybersecurity ETF
CIBR.text: Another fund focused on the cybersecurity industry.

BTC.name: Bitcoin
BTC.text: The first and best-known cryptocurrency — digital money with no central bank.

ETH.name: Ethereum
ETH.text: A cryptocurrency and platform used to build many other apps and tokens.

SOL.name: Solana
SOL.text: A cryptocurrency known for fast and cheap transactions.

BNB.name: BNB
BNB.text: The cryptocurrency of the large Binance exchange, also used to pay fees on it.

XRP.name: XRP
XRP.text: A cryptocurrency originally built for fast international money transfers.

ADA.name: Cardano
ADA.text: A cryptocurrency and blockchain platform that emphasizes a research-driven approach to development.

SPY.name: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust
SPY.text: One of the most popular funds in the world — a single purchase gives you a stake in the 500 largest US companies.

VOO.name: Vanguard S&P 500 ETF
VOO.text: Another fund tracking the same S&P 500 index, with a low fee.

VTI.name: Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF
VTI.text: A fund covering almost the entire US stock market — not just large companies, but mid- and small-caps too.

QQQ.name: Invesco QQQ Trust (Nasdaq-100)
QQQ.text: A fund of the 100 largest non-financial companies on the Nasdaq exchange — heavy on tech.

DIA.name: SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF
DIA.text: A fund tracking one of the oldest US indexes — 30 large industrial and consumer companies.

IWM.name: iShares Russell 2000 ETF
IWM.text: A fund of two thousand small-cap US companies — that is, smaller than giants like Apple.

BND.name: Vanguard Total Bond Market ETF
BND.text: A fund covering a broad range of US bonds — a one-click way to add the calm part of a portfolio.

AGG.name: iShares Core U.S. Aggregate Bond ETF
AGG.text: Another large fund covering the broad US bond market.

TLT.name: iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF
TLT.text: A fund of long-term US government bonds — usually the most sensitive to changes in interest rates.

IEF.name: iShares 7-10 Year Treasury Bond ETF
IEF.text: A fund of US government bonds with medium-term maturities.

SHY.name: iShares 1-3 Year Treasury Bond ETF
SHY.text: A fund of short-term US government bonds — considered one of the calmest options around.

LQD.name: iShares iBoxx $ Investment Grade Corp Bond ETF
LQD.text: A fund of bonds from large companies with solid credit ratings.

VNQ.name: Vanguard Real Estate ETF
VNQ.text: A fund of shares in companies that own shopping malls, warehouses, housing, and other real estate.
